item.title: ‘Hub for change’: Obama Presidential Center to open in 2026 – What visitors can expect
item.description: Chicago's historic Jackson Park is set to welcome the Obama Presidential Center next year, a vibrant hub for culture and community. The 19-acre campus, featuring a museum opening in 2026, aims to inspire global visitors and local residents alike. With public gardens, a library, and multipurpose spaces, the center promises significant economic impact and a strong focus on sustainability.

item.title: Fans call to shut down TwitchCon after shocking attack on streamer Emiru

Twitch responded by banning the assailant and increasing security, but many remain skeptical.

item.title: As social media grills Pete Hegseth for 'Russian tie', JD Vance defends him: 'Maybe he was wearing...'
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance defended Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after a social media storm erupted over his tie's colors, perceived by some as resembling the Russian flag during a meeting with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy. Vance suggested the tie represented American colors, but many remained unconvinced, citing product listings describing it as a 'Russian plain flag tie'.

item.title: “Trans activism is my purpose”: Lia Thomas sparks controversy after accepting an LGBTQIA+ award
item.description: Lia Thomas, the first transgender NCAA women's swimming champion, received the Voice of Inspiration Award, sparking renewed debate on transgender athletes. Her acceptance speech, framing trans activism as her purpose, drew praise from supporters and sharp criticism from opponents like swimmer Riley Gaines, who deemed it an 'insult to women' and a dismissal of fair competition standards.

item.title: Twitch streamer Emiru reportedly assaulted during TwitchCon meet-and-greet event
item.description: A disturbing incident at TwitchCon 2025 saw popular streamer Emiru allegedly assaulted during a meet-and-greet. A viral clip sparked outrage, prompting Twitch to ban the attendee indefinitely and increase security. However, critics argue the response is too late, especially after Emiru was reportedly denied a personal bodyguard, reigniting creator safety concerns.

item.title: From 'Orange Lies Matter' to 'Make Fascists Afraid Again': 10 placards that stole the show at 'No Kings' protest
item.description: Millions are preparing for a second wave of "No Kings" protests across the US, opposing President Trump's "authoritarian" agenda. Following numerous executive orders and federal actions, over 2,500 rallies are planned nationwide. Organizers emphasize peaceful demonstrations against authoritarianism, corruption, and threats to civil liberties.

item.title: Sharjah: Mohammed Bin Musa Al Khwarizmi road remains closed until October 19
item.description: Mohammed Bin Musa Al Khwarizmi Road in Sharjah, near University Hospital, has been temporarily closed by the Sharjah Roads and Transport Authority for essential maintenance. The closure began on October 17 and will continue until October 19. Alternative routes have been provided, and motorists are urged to follow safety guidelines and traffic instructions during this period.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Love America, hate Trump: 'No Kings' rallies across US diss Donald
item.description: Millions of Americans protested across the country in a "No Kings" movement against President Trump’s perceived authoritarianism. Demonstrators criticised his immigration policies, militarisation of cities, and federal overreach. Trump and allies dismissed them as “hate America rallies” by radicals. Despite deep divisions, protests remained largely peaceful, with witty slogans and satire urging focus on domestic issues and democratic values.

item.title: Zero personal income tax: Poland introduces new law for parents with two children – What it means for families
item.description: Poland's President Karol Nawrocki has approved a new law eliminating personal income tax for parents with at least two children, aiming to boost household income and stimulate the economy. This tax relief, applicable to families earning up to 140,000 zloty annually, is expected to benefit families significantly, though experts suggest wealthier households will see the greatest gains.

item.title: What are ‘No Kings’ protests? Why thousands are rallying against Trump and how the MAGA regime is fighting back
item.description: Thousands of Americans are set to protest nationwide against President Donald Trump and his policies on Saturday, with over 2,500 rallies planned. Organizers, including prominent Democrats, aim to present a unified opposition to what they call Trump's authoritarianism. Republican leaders have dismissed the demonstrations as radical and linked to far-left groups, with some governors activating the National Guard.

item.title: Canada announces investigation into paper plates; Social media users troll govt; 'Feeling very much safe'
item.description: The Canada Border Service Agency is investigating whether China is dumping disposable paper plates and bowls, potentially harming Canadian industries. This announcement sparked widespread mockery on social media, with critics questioning the focus on paper plates over more pressing issues like fentanyl and illegal guns.

item.title: Justin Trudeau dating Katy Perry: Why people love Mills & Boons yacht romances
item.description: This isn’t simply a pop star dating a politician. Trudeau is one of the most recognisable political figures of his generation — a man who reshaped Canada’s global identity, embodied progressive politics, and, for a time, symbolised the liberal response to Donald Trump. Perry, meanwhile, was once one of the most dominant cultural forces in music. Their union is more than a tabloid headline; it’s a sign of how celebrity has colonised politics — and how political figures now compete with entertainers not just for power, but for relevance.
